results.summary_before: This project implements a programmable chaotic random number generator based on a 3D double-scroll chaotic map. It uses three 32-bit state variables updated each clock cycle with arithmetic feedback and nonlinear functions, producing an 8-bit random output. The chaotic parameters are partially programmable via input pins, allowing configuration of the nonlinear function. No external hardware is required, and the design is documented with details on its internal state and programmability.

results.summary_before: This project is a tetrahedral-style oscillator built from coupled CMOS inverter pairs with MIM capacitors as load elements, implemented in the SKY130 process. It provides four buffered observation outputs that oscillate around 12 MHz when powered from a 1.8 V supply. The design is tested by probing the outputs with a high-impedance oscilloscope or frequency counter, and no external passives or bias sources are needed. Post-layout extracted simulation was performed to verify oscillation.

results.summary_before: tinyCGRA 2x2 is a 2x2 coarse-grained reconfigurable array where each processing element selects two of four neighbour inputs and applies a 2-bit ALU operation. Configuration is shifted in serially as a 24-bit bitstream, and a latched input byte is broadcast to the north and west edges while the output pins show one selected PE result or an XOR of all four. The repository also includes generic 3x3 and multi-context variants for area studies. It is tested through a Tiny Tapeout top regression and separate area-top regressions.

results.summary_before: This is an unmanaged 3-port 100 Mbps Ethernet switch implemented in Verilog, using RMII interfaces to connect to external PHYs. It performs cut-through switching between the three ports, with two ports on dedicated pins and one on bidirectional pins. The design requires external Ethernet PHY hardware, such as LAN8720A modules, and a 50 MHz oscillator. It is a complex networking design that fits in a 2x2 tile area and is intended for hardware testing with real network traffic.

results.summary_before: This project implements a single-rounded bfloat16 fused multiply-add (FMA) unit with a byte-serial I/O interface. It uses a six-stage pipeline to reduce the critical path delay, which is particularly useful because the limited I/O requires three clock cycles to load each set of operands. The design handles special values such as zero, infinity, and NaN, and rounds results using round-to-nearest, ties-to-even. It is intended for integration into larger systems and requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout interface.
